lines.t: Hi everyone, and welcome to the SpeakLab Podcast. I'm Leyla.
And I'm Sam. Today's topic is gifts and giving. And I need your help, Leyla.
Why?
It's my mum's birthday next week, and I have no idea what to buy.
What does she like?
Gardening, tea, and calling me every evening. [laugh]
Then something thoughtful. Maybe a nice tea set from Baku, with armudu glasses.
Perfect! But I'm terrible at wrapping presents. Last year my present looked like a used bag.
The shop can wrap it for you. And honestly, it's the thought that counts.
You know what surprised me here? When I gave Mr Aliyev a small gift, he said no twice.
Ah, yes. Many people refuse a gift once or twice — it's just polite. You have to insist.
I had no idea! I almost took it back home.
[chuckle] And he's very generous himself, isn't he?
Very. Every week he brings me apples and figs from his garden. It's a lovely gesture.
My niece Aysu made me a birthday card last month. Glitter everywhere, and a cat with six legs.
That's the best kind of gift.
It is. It's on my fridge. Now tell me about your half marathon — I heard it's for charity?
Yes! Our running club is raising money for a children's hospital. People donate for every kilometre.
That's wonderful. I'll donate too. You always go the extra mile, Sam.
Twenty-one kilometres, actually. [laugh] Thank you!
Here's your question for your next SpeakLab call: what is the best gift you have ever received — and why was it special?
Mine is a bag of figs from my neighbour. See you next time!
Bye for now!
